display_name: Credit points under Income Tax Ordinance ss 33A, 34, 36 and 36A: the credit point and allowance point, two points for an Israeli resident individual, a quarter point travel credit, and half a point for a woman

language.note: English identifiers (@lang en); the Hebrew of every provision is quoted in inert strings and comments, rendered mechanically from the deposited source by render_source.py, which also checks every quotation (`python3 -I render_source.py --check *.l4`).

scope: Encoded: s 33A (the definitions of 'נקודת זיכוי' -- NIS 504 per tax year, indexed, set off against that year's tax -- and of 'נקודת קיצבה' -- the 31 December 1996 credit point as adjusted under s 120B, divided by twelve), s 34 (two points for an individual who was an Israeli resident in the tax year), s 36 (a quarter point 'as a travel credit' for an Israeli resident individual), s 36A (half a point for a woman), and the aggregate 'credit points under ss 34 and 36' that s 134A(2) names. Taken as inputs, with no default: the year's indexed credit-point value (s 120B, row IL-03), the tax it is set off against (s 121 etc., row IL-03), and Israeli residence for the tax year (s 1, not encoded). Reached and refused: s 48 (order of 5755-1995 for Area residents who are not Israeli citizens) and s 48A (Regulations of 5775-2014 for foreign workers), wherever either could decide the answer. Not encoded: ss 35, 37-48A and the rest of Part C Chapter Three (row IL-08 and others), s 66 (row IL-02), ss 120B, 121, 121B (row IL-03). Published Israel Tax Authority figures (NIS 2,904 per point for 2025; NIS 242 per point per month for 2024-2026) are carried in a separate module, labelled as published figures and not as law. Law stated as the Wikisource consolidation retrieved 2026-10-06; the slice carries no dated arm, and is assumed (not verified against the amending Acts) to have stood since the 5764 (2003-04) amendment to s 33A.

inputs.published_figures: Israel Tax Authority form 135 notes for 2025 (sha256 207412d97ed3daa65f49d42ae7e68e62e67e1f0dba674be40962989f7c9ad0eb) and monthly withholding booklets 2024-2026; URLs, archive captures and hashes in ito-credit-points-published-figures.l4

not_reviewed.note: No domain expert has read this encoding against the source. No independent test pass has been run (the row was produced in one session, without sub-agents, at the lead's instruction). Every expected value in the tests was written from the source text or the Tax Authority's published statement, by the same session that wrote the rules.

self_check.result: 5 modules, 0 errors, 58 assertions satisfied, 0 failed, 0 refused

forks.F1: s 36A has no residence limb (unlike ss 34 and 36), and s 48 does not list it: read literally, a non-resident woman gets half a point.
forks.F2: s 36's heading speaks of travel to the place of earning; its body imposes no condition of earning or travel: the body is followed, every resident individual gets the quarter point.
forks.F3: s 36 says 'יחיד תושב ישראל' without 'in the tax year': read as the same residence-for-the-tax-year as s 34.
forks.F4: Part-year residence: residence is one status per tax year, supplied by the caller; no apportionment by this row.
forks.F5: 'המקוזז כנגד המס לאותה שנה': the credit reduces that year's tax to no less than zero; no refund, no carry-over (supported by s 91's 'יתרת נקודות הזיכוי').
forks.F6: s 33A indexes 'as stated in s 120A', whose definition of 'מדד' is deleted; s 120B is read as governing. No answer turns on it, because the indexed value is an input.
forks.F7: Wikisource editorial figures are not law and are not used as values.
forks.F8: The points are 'taken into account' with no claim or proof: an entitlement computed from facts, not a deontic permission.
forks.F10: Where s 48 or s 48A could decide the case the model refuses, rather than answering as if the instrument did not exist or from an editor's summary of it.
